column2: Experienced hunters are often recruited into local formations of Caçadores due to their proficient at the use of the bow and arrow as well as superb quality as ambushers.
It is in those camps where the armies of Iberia train their 'Rodeleros', shock infantry formations who are often used to break the stalemate of battles and named after their use of the Rodelo shied.

Andalusian horses are renowed all over the world as some of the best cavalry in the world, a fact which doesn't go unnoticed by Andalusians nobles, who take their sons young age to the equestrian schools where they learn from a young age the art of riding those formidable horses.

Heavily armed with battle axes and armoured with plumed helmets, the Sapeurs de la Garde specialize in military engineering and underground combat, though they can also serve as an elite corps of provisional infantry.

Skilled sailors and consummate ambushers, the mariners of Brittany's coasts are as fearless on land as on sea. Whether it is a quick strike on an undefended target or a more protacted battle, they shall respond to the call. Kentoc'h mervel!

These isolated camps, usually in the forest, provide the perfect locale for the lifeblood of Welsh and Cornish sovereignty, where they could train, produce weaponry for their militia and learn to live off the land, away from the prying eyes of lords and kings, be they foreign or domestic.

Albeit Leagues were once spoken of a sport that caused peasants to go mad and cause immense damage, these Leaguers are war camps established by British lords to hone and prepare men who would use the halberd-like weaponry to wild success against both raiders from the rest of the Isles and foreign conquerors who dared to enter a struggle against Queen and Country.

The schiltron is a compact body of Scottish pikemen. If threatened by cavalry, they present row upon row of spears firmly braced in the earth. Only a fool or a madman would willingly charge into such a dense wall of killing instruments.

Civilian housing repurposed for the residence of these plaid-laden, barefooted warriors, primarily with the peasantry in them still. They are primarily displeased at them, but aren't to complain due to their extreme resilience even in the coldest weather and the fact that they are armed troops.

The Gewalthaufen is a shambling mass of pikes and halberds, the men usually protected by a ridged helmet and a cuirass. Flags, drums and horns coordinate the formation so that the officers with with decorated helmets can move hundreds of men with one word. This of course needs a rather high amount of training and equipment which is why the local authorities like to keep a training ground and a stockpile of equipment around.
